sessions.feedback: Digest 'biggest pre-market movers' ranks thin prints (100-600 shares) by sd, so most of the list is noise (e.g., KNX -8.5% on 396 shares). Filtering on minimum shares or a percent-of-average-day threshold would save budget. A tool returning the biggest losers and gainers of the previous session (not only gainers) would help find overreactions. A 'peers with earnings dates in the next 5 days' lookup by industry would suit the lagging-peer strategy.

Benzinga pages usually fail in read_page, though the digest links mostly point to Benzinga. Pre-market lists mix thin prints with real moves (e.g. NX -19% in the news roundup versus 0.0% in scan). Some prices look like spin-off artifacts (CTVA 9.43, -90% from 52-week high); a flag for corporate actions would help.

read_page fails on many major sites (CNBC, NBC, gurufocus), which makes the two-source requirement hard. The sandbox does not keep Python state between code_execution cells, so imports have to be repeated in every cell. A pre-market quote that shows volume (e.g. 828 shares) makes thin-volume REIT quotes misleading; a flag for low-volume pre-market prints would help.

The digest has no sector or industry-level sympathy view and the scan's industry labels are coarse (e.g. UBER/LYFT listed as 'Business Services'). Web search returns stale results for some queries. Earnings-call transcripts or a news-by-ticker endpoint would help.

summary:
Session 2026-11-17.

Session 2026-11-17. Portfolio stays 100% cash and I placed no trades. SPY fell 1.9% and QQQ 2.7% on 11-16. Pre-market is flat to slightly up, with NVDA earnings after the close and an Anthropic IPO to follow. Cash is a sound default into those binary events.

I checked these leads:
- Nvidia scandal and the 11-16 Commerce chip rule. It needs licenses for advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, and for data centers giving China-HQ firms large remote access, with a 90-day clock. US-HQ buyers are exempt. The first-order reaction is already priced: GDS fell 14.7% in the US, Malaysian data-center stocks fell about 20% in Asia, and the NVDA customer exposure is at most 1.3% of revenue.
- Home Depot. Revenue and comps beat (2.2% vs 1.8%), but LOW has already run 15% in 20 days.
- TJX. It reports 11-18 BMO and has sold off into the print. I judged it a coin flip with no edge.
- AECOM. It is up about 6.5% pre-market on record backlog, and its peers are not laggards.
- Amer Sports. It raised guidance, and I found no peer catalyst.
- TU, BCE and RCI. All priced.
- JPM bank outages. A JPM internal bug, with no vendor named.
- Berkshire 13F. The only new name is Bending Spoons.
- Oil and tankers. Brent is about $92 as Hormuz flows normalize, but the direction for tankers is unclear.
- Thin pre-market prints. The KNX, NX, HTLD and SR moves are noise, since they came on a few hundred shares.

Next session (11-18):
- Read the NVDA print and its reaction.
- Look for a PUBM-style trade: a lagging peer with a dated catalyst.
- Check how the TJX, LOW and TGT results move ROST and BURL.
- Check how Anthropic (ANT) prices on the evening of 11-18, and how AMZN and GOOGL trade on it.
- Check Warsh's comments.
- Upcoming dates: PANW 11-18 AMC; WMT, KEYS and INTU 11-19; BSP and FRO 11-20; DELL and BURL 11-24.

- Nvidia saga: Huang resigned 11-12 (spy/Megaspeed diversion scandal), Kress interim CEO; NVDA earnings 11-17 AMC (consensus rev $108.8B, EPS $2.47, implied move ~9%; stock 156, lowest close since Jul 2025). On 11-16 Commerce issued an interim rule: licenses for advanced chips to Singapore/Malaysia/Thailand/Indonesia/Brazil (US-HQ companies exempt with reporting) + license for data centers giving China-HQ firms >12M TPP remote access, 90-day clock. Rules rescinds AI Diffusion Rule. Malaysian data-center stocks -20% in Asia, GDS -14.7% in US 11-16 (priced). NVDA customers in the 5 countries at most 1.3% of revenue. APEC Trump-Xi in Shenzhen starts 11-18. Anthropic (ticker ANT) IPO prices 11-18 evening, trades Nasdaq 11-19, range $70-78, ~$64B raise, valuation $1.0-1.4T; AMZN holds ~14.7%, GOOGL ~13.7%. SpaceX already listed (SPCX, cap ~$1.9T).
- Trades so far: only PUBM (11-06 long 4%, closed 11-13 +12.5%, +9.9 pts vs SPY). Worked because peer lagged leader and had a dated catalyst.
- Sessions with no trade: 10-29, 11-04, 11-16, 11-17 (cash vs falling SPY has been the right default; SPY -1.9% on 11-16).
- 11-17 candidates looked at and rejected: HD (rev beat, comps 2.2% vs 1.8%, CEO change; LOW reports 11-18, +15% 20d already), TJX (reports 11-18 BMO; guided EPS $1.30-1.32 ex tariff-refund, cons $1.33; fell 5 days, -11% 20d, PT cuts and two downgrades into print; IEEPA tariff refunds help Q3; weak edge so skipped, coin flip), ACM (+6.5% pre on record backlog; peers J/TTEK not laggards), AS (raised guide, +5% pre, no peer catalyst), TU/BCE/RCI (priced, TU closed +12%, BCE +3.3%, RCI +4.2%), bank outages (JPM internal bug, no vendor named), Berkshire 13F (only new name Bending Spoons BSP, Lennar nearly doubled), tankers FRO/DHT/INSW (Hormuz normalizing; FRO reports 11-20, direction unclear), GDS/VNET (priced).
- Lesson: By the pre-open session, first-order and obvious second-order moves are priced (GDS fell 14.7% a day before I looked). Prefer peers with an upcoming catalyst that lagged the leader (earnings read-through), or overreactions after multi-day diffusion. Cash is measured against SPY too.

prompt:
Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is weird, second-order research.

Everyone else reads the headline and trades the company in it. You trade the company the headline
does not mention. Start from events in the news and follow the consequences outward: suppliers,
customers, competitors, substitutes, regions, commodities, logistics, weather, regulation, the
odd dependency nobody has priced. A storm hits the region that grows potatoes for a fast-food chain;
which other chain gains, which frozen-food maker loses, which railroad hauls the replacement crop?

- Every new position, long or short, needs a causal chain of at least two steps from the event to
  the company you trade, each step with a source where possible. Code rejects a trade whose ticker
  or company name appears in today's digest headlines, so the link has to be one you found. The
  losers at the end of a chain are as fair game as the winners: short them.
- Borderline delusional is the brief, but the chain still has to be real: each step should be
  something you could defend with evidence. Write down the step most likely to be wrong.
- Spreading across several smaller bets suits this style better than one big one. Small companies
  cost more to trade, so make the expected move worth it.
- Use search_symbols to find the companies at the end of a chain. Read their exposure, do not assume it.
